reviewer: Independent spire_verify agent; geometry and rendered images inspected
scope: Actual Blender PNG inspection only; not native Studio, device, human art or world completion acceptance
findings: Matched spire_reveal and native_road_eye show a recognizable ruined masonry tower replacing the plain faceted beacon; both open arch tiers and broken crown remain legible at route distance.
close_front and close_side show stone courses, arch voussoirs, stepped buttresses and an irregular crown. The full crown is now inside the side view.
The repaired buttress feet reach the slope. Independent geometry audit separately confirms 72 outer-foot, 25 primary-foundation and 15 fallen-stone support rays.
base_detail now exposes three moss-topped fallen blocks and small accents against the footing; the earlier bare-plinth view has improved.
Visible road sightline and lane composition remain open in both matched route views.
remainingGaps: The fallen blocks form a neat short row; their ruin composition is still modest and does not yet establish a larger collapsed architectural remnant.
Vegetation accents at the base are tiny and partially buried/occluded in these views; biome weathering is not a strong visual feature.
The broad surrounding slopes, sparse repeated trees and long simple water boundary remain visibly unfinished.
Stone palette and repeated ashlar rhythm remain uniform; more deliberate damage and material aging could improve close inspection.
close_side is reframed to fit the repaired structure, so the same-camera before/after claim is limited to the two route views explicitly inspected here.
City/Greenwood surroundings in these Blender images are schematic and do not prove native-world integration.
